title: Division and inverses
goal: Use a⁻¹, use "if ab = 0, then a = 0 or b = 0", and solve equations with fractions.
generalHint: Check the signs. Multiply both sides by the inverse. A denominator must not be 0.

options.label: Yes, it is a fraction
options.reply: Theorem 4 says that no positive rational number has the square 2. Can √2 be a fraction?

feedback.correctWhy: By Theorem 4, no fraction m/n has the square 2. So √2 is irrational.

screens.label: PUZZLE
screens.title: Back to 1
screens.prompt: Find the number you multiply by 2/3 to get exactly 1. You can type a fraction.

answer.correctWhy: (2/3)(3/2) = 6/6 = 1. The number 3/2 is 2/3 turned upside down.

mistakes.reply: That is the same number. Multiply 2/3 by it. Is the result 1?

mistakes.reply: That cancels the 3s but not the 2s. Multiply the tops, then the bottoms.

screens.label: NAME IT
screens.title: The inverse
screens.prompt: For a rational number $a \ne 0$, the number $a^{-1}$ is the multiplicative inverse: $a a^{-1} = 1$. If $a = m/n$, then $a^{-1} = n/m$.

note.label: WORDS MATTER
note.text: a⁻¹ is the inverse of a, not "a to the minus one" yet. The number 0 has no inverse.

screens.label: PROVE IT
screens.title: The inverse is unique
screens.prompt: Prove: if $ab = 1$, then $b = a^{-1}$. Multiply both sides by $a^{-1}$.

wrongReasonReplies.inverse-exists: This rule says a · a⁻¹ = 1. Is there a product of a and a⁻¹ in the line before?
wrongReasonReplies.assoc-mul: Associativity changes the brackets in a product of three factors. Did the brackets change?
wrongReasonReplies.N6: N6 says 1a = a. Is there a 1 times a number to change?
wrongReasonReplies.comm-mul: Commutativity changes the order of two factors. Did the order change in this line?
wrongReasonReplies.distrib: Distributivity splits a(b + c). Is there a sum in brackets here?
wrongReasonReplies.mult-both: This step multiplies both sides by the same number. Did this line multiply both sides?

feedback.correctWhy: If two numbers multiply to 1, each is the inverse of the other. So the inverse is unique.

screens.label: PROVE IT
screens.title: A product of 0
screens.prompt: Prove: if $ab = 0$ and $a \ne 0$, then $b = 0$. Multiply both sides by $a^{-1}$.

wrongReasonReplies.inverse-exists: This rule says a · a⁻¹ = 1. Is there a product of a and a⁻¹ in the line before?
wrongReasonReplies.assoc-mul: Associativity changes the brackets in a product of three factors. Did the brackets change?
wrongReasonReplies.N6: N6 says 1a = a. Is there a 1 times a number to change?
wrongReasonReplies.comm-mul: Commutativity changes the order of two factors. Did the order change in this line?
wrongReasonReplies.distrib: Distributivity splits a(b + c). Is there a sum in brackets here?
wrongReasonReplies.mult-both: This step multiplies both sides by the same number. Did this line multiply both sides?
wrongReasonReplies.zero-mul: This rule says 0a = 0. Is there a 0 times a number in the line before?

feedback.correctWhy: If ab = 0, then a = 0 or b = 0. We showed: if a is not 0, then b is 0.

screens.label: USE IT
screens.title: Solve by factoring
screens.prompt: Use "if ab = 0, then a = 0 or b = 0" for the equation $x(x - 3) = 0$.

options.label: $x = 3$ only
options.reply: If x = 0, then x(x − 3) = 0 · (−3) = 0. Is x = 0 a solution too?

options.label: $x = 0$ only
options.reply: If x = 3, then x(x − 3) = 3 · 0 = 0. Is x = 3 a solution too?

feedback.correctWhy: A product is 0 only if one factor is 0. So x = 0 or x − 3 = 0, that is x = 3.

hints: A product is 0 if one factor is 0.

screens.label: NAME IT
screens.title: Quotients
screens.prompt: For rational numbers $a$ and $b \ne 0$, we write $a/b$ for $b^{-1}a$.

options.label: $a^{-1}b$
options.reply: In a/b, the letter b is below the line. Which letter has the −1?

feedback.correctWhy: a/b is the number b⁻¹ times a. For example 3/4 = 4⁻¹ · 3.

screens.label: PROVE IT
screens.title: Cross−multiplication
screens.prompt: Lesson 1.6 assumed the cross−multiplication rule. Now prove it: if $a/b = c/d$, then $ad = bc$.

wrongReasonReplies.inverse-exists: This rule says a · a⁻¹ = 1. Is there a number times its inverse in the line before?
wrongReasonReplies.assoc-mul: Associativity changes the brackets in a product of three factors. Did the brackets change?
wrongReasonReplies.comm-mul: Commutativity changes the order of factors. Did the order change?
wrongReasonReplies.N6: N6 says 1a = a. Is there a 1 times a number to change?
wrongReasonReplies.def-frac: This step writes a/b as b⁻¹a. Is there a quotient in the line before?
wrongReasonReplies.mult-both: This step multiplies both sides by the same number. Did this line multiply both sides?
wrongReasonReplies.cancel-mul: This law removes a common factor from both sides. Is there a common factor a ≠ 0 on both sides?

feedback.correctWhy: bb⁻¹ = 1 and dd⁻¹ = 1. So da = bc, which is ad = bc.

screens.caption: Tap a reason to fill the orange slot.

screens.label: NAME IT
screens.title: The cancellation law
screens.prompt: If $a \ne 0$ and $ab = ac$, then $b = c$. Multiply both sides by $a^{-1}$. A denominator must not be 0.

note.label: REMEMBER
note.text: Fractions add like this: a/b + c/d = (ad + bc)/bd. The numbers b and d must not be 0.

screens.label: EXPLORE
screens.title: Solve by cross−multiplying
screens.prompt: Solve $3/(x + 2) = 4$. Cross−multiply: $3 = 4(x + 2)$. Find $x$. You can type a fraction.

mistakes.reply: Multiply 4 by both x and 2: 4(x + 2) = 4x + 8. What is 3 − 8?
The sign is wrong. Check: if x = 5/4, then x + 2 = 13/4. Is 3 divided by 13/4 equal to 4?

screens.label: EXPLORE
screens.title: Speed, distance and time
screens.prompt: The formula is $d = st$. A cyclist goes 6 km in 3/4 hour. Find the speed in km per hour.

mistakes.reply: That multiplies 6 by 3/4. The speed is distance divided by time: s = d/t.
That is t/d turned the wrong way. The speed is d/t. What is 6 divided by 3/4?

hints: Dividing by 3/4 is the same as multiplying by 4/3.

screens.label: PRACTICE · 2 OF 2
screens.title: Walk and cycle
screens.prompt: You walk at 3 km/h and cycle at 15 km/h. In 2 hours you go 18 km. Find the cycle time in hours.

mistakes.reply: Check: cycling 1.5 hours is 22.5 km. That is more than 18 km. Use 15t + 3(2 − t) = 18.
That is the whole time. You walk part of the time too. Use 15t + 3(2 − t) = 18.

hints: Let t be the cycle time. The walk time is 2 − t.

trap.question: True or false: x² = 3x. Divide by x, so x = 3 is the only solution.

options.label: True
options.reply: If x = 0, you cannot divide by x. Move all terms to one side and factor.

feedback.correctWhy: x = 0 is also a solution. Write x² − 3x = 0, so x(x − 3) = 0. Then x = 0 or x = 3.
